issues.detail: The Greek 'ποιο' (poion) is an interrogative pronoun meaning 'which', but the Vietnamese translation treats it as a relative pronoun or part of a descriptive phrase ('sự chết nào' - 'the death which'). More importantly, the Greek structure 'δε ελεγεν σημαινων ποιω θανατω' implies 'He did not say [it] meaning which death,' but the Vietnamese 'để chỉ về' (to point to/refer to) changes the logical connection from a negation of intent to a statement of purpose.
